Alternate Name: Bohada Mask Festival / Tribal Mask Festival
Village: Mokhada, Bharsat Meth, Kardan, Denga chi Meth, Vehel Pada, Jawhar, Poyshet, Kokada
Deity: Gaon Devi and other Gods and Goddesses
Historical Background: Traditional tribal mask festival of the Thane and Nashik region. Mokhada is considered the birthplace of Bohada, while Bharsat Meth is famous for its celebration.
Rituals: Rice seedlings are grown seven days before the festival and offered to Gaon Devi. Mask owners wear the masks and perform during the three-day festival.
Fair Activities: Display and procession of 52 masks, folk dance, traditional music, mythological performances and community gatherings
Cultural Significance: Preserves tribal mythology, traditional mask-making, folk arts, music, dance, oral traditions and indigenous cultural identity
Source: https://dsource.in/resource/tribal-paper-mache-mask/bohada-festival
